entities.title: Ram Nath Adhikari

properties.profile: Agriculture and Livestock Development Minister from the Nepali Congress. Resigned on 9 September 2025, saying he acted on moral grounds and to object to the government's actions. Republica reports he stepped down after party leader Shekhar Koirala directed his faction's ministers to quit.

entities.title: Pradip Paudel

properties.profile: Health and Population Minister. Announced on 9 September 2025 that he was stepping down. Kantipur lists him as the fourth minister to resign after Lekhak, Chaudhary and Adhikari. Spelled Poudel in some reports.

entities.title: Tejulal Chaudhary

properties.profile: Youth and Sports Minister in the Oli cabinet. Resigned on 9 September 2025 after the use of force against the protests.

evidence.note: Name spelling follows Republica; Kantipur gives only the surname.

entities.title: Pradip Yadav

properties.profile: Water Supply Minister and deputy general secretary of the Janata Samajwadi Party. Announced on Facebook on 9 September 2025 that he was resigning in support of the protests and against the crackdown.

entities.title: Deepak Khadka

properties.profile: Energy Minister. Setopati reports his home was vandalised on the morning of 9 September 2025.

entities.title: Bishwa Prakash Sharma

properties.profile: Nepali Congress general secretary. With Gagan Thapa he demanded Home Minister Lekhak's resignation on 8 September 2025 and, on 9 September, that the party recall its ministers from the Oli government.

entities.title: Rajyalaxmi Chitrakar

properties.profile: Wife of former prime minister Jhalanath Khanal. Injured with burns when the family home in Dallu was set on fire on 9 September 2025. Also written Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar. Some outlets reported her dead on 9 September; fact-checkers and Setopati said she was alive. She returned home after treatment in Delhi in December 2025.

evidence.note: Identified only as named in reporting. Her death was reported by some outlets on 9 September and contradicted by BOOM, Alt News and Setopati; see claims.

entities.title: Oli resigns as prime minister

properties.summary: KP Sharma Oli submitted his resignation to President Ram Chandra Paudel on Tuesday afternoon under Article 77(1)(a) of the Constitution. The Prime Minister's Secretariat confirmed it and the President accepted it the same afternoon. Himalayan Times pages are stamped 14:31 (resignation) and 15:03 (acceptance).

evidence.property: summary, when, precision, event_type, phase, verification
evidence.note: Hour not stated for the submission itself; only 'Tuesday afternoon'. The 14:31 and 15:03 values are the Himalayan Times page timestamps.

entities.title: Security chiefs tell Oli they cannot guarantee citizens' safety

properties.summary: Himal Press reports that Army chief Ashok Raj Sigdel, Inspector General Chandra Kuber Khapung and Armed Police Force head Raju Aryal briefed Oli that they could not guarantee citizens' safety if he stayed in office. Oli first said he would not resign.

evidence.property: summary, when, precision, event_type, phase, verification
evidence.note: Single outlet. Not found in other retrievable coverage.

evidence.property: summary, when, precision, event_type, phase, verification

properties.summary: Setopati reports the army flew Oli from Baluwatar by helicopter immediately after his resignation, and that Dahal and Madhav Kumar Nepal were flown from Singha Durbar.
